sourceFacts.fact: HUS involves red-cell destruction, low platelet count and acute kidney injury.
Microvascular damage links red-cell fragmentation, platelet consumption and impaired kidney function.

layout: A top-centre blue node1 branches into THREE equal, clearly separated vertical columns. Left column node2 then3, centre node4 then5, right node6 then7. Exactly six connectors and seven labelled nodes, no cross-links. Neutral metaphors: torn red paper discs for fragmentation, fewer ochre dot tokens for consumption, and an abstract declining gauge for function. No red-cell microscopy, platelets with anatomical detail, vessel or kidney icon. Below the columns print: The haemolytic uraemic syndrome triad.

requiredChecks: Exactly three branches from one central process
Each mechanism links only to its matched outcome
Low platelets follow consumption and anaemia follows red-cell fragmentation
No vessels, organs, cells or clinical smear
validation.pixelChecks: Pixel review: seven nodes and six directed links form three correctly matched HUS branches. Torn red paper tokens, ochre inventory tokens and gauges stay abstract; no vascular or organ anatomy. Top microvascular heading and bottom triad heading carry the intended teaching point although the requested introductory title was omitted. Clinical and independent review pending.
